title: Painel 3 CBSoft 2026:  Navigating the Uncharted Implications of Advanced Artificial Intelligence in Software Engineering - Sala Alan Turing (Auditório FAU)
description:
Advanced Artificial Intelligence (AI) techniques — such as deep learning, foundation models, agentic systems and multiagent systems — are increasingly used for improving automation across the software lifecycle. While these techniques may accelerate software production, their inherent characteristics, including autonomy, opacity, generative capabilities, and non-determinism, may impose understudied or unmapped risks to both software quality and engineering teams. Understanding and managing these risks is particularly critical in contexts that demand strict guarantees around dependability, performance and developer well-being. Bringing together experts in complementary research topics, this panel aims to address four questions:
  1. Understudied Factors: Which software quality and human factors impacted by AI remain understudied? How are they possibly impacted?
  2. Unmapped Risks: What are the less-understood risks that characteristics of advanced AI techniques impose on software quality and human factors?
  3. Underexplored Opportunities: Which capabilities of these techniques (and why) should be better leveraged to further improve software quality and team work?
  4. Longitudinal Research: How can we design and conduct rigorous long-term studies to better measure AI impact on software maintenance, evolution and developer well-being?
